findings.reason: without a fourth source named and a precedence that covers it, a node cannot compute the unit's five census figures or decide which unit to store, and the delivered census would be internally unreconcilable with the stored property.
findings.text: §11's source list and its unit rules do not compose: the three deciding sources are "the field pattern of its name, the controls metadata it already carries, or a linked signal-list row", yet the very next sentence treats "the units a signal already carries from the archive and the controls metadata" as authoritative and requires "the assigned unit equals it for every such signal". A unit that only the archive supplies therefore has no bucket among the three sources, so it is counted undecided while the assignment is required to preserve it; and where a linked row's unit differs from the archive's, the added precedence order credits the row while the equality clause — seeing only the archive as giving a unit — demands the archive's value, so two rules require two different stored units for one signal

findings.reason: the mixed case is the one the pilot's 190 row-linked signals can actually present (a row plus controls metadata plus a field pattern), and the two readings put those signals in different census buckets, so the five figures summing to 1,766 and the conflict count are not determined by the plan text.
findings.text: the credit rule and the conflict bucket both claim the same case: a value "that more than one source decides alike is credited to the first of them in the order linked signal-list row, controls metadata, field pattern", while the conflict figure counts a value "because its sources disagree" and the negative control says "a signal whose sources disagree on the plan's unit is recorded as a conflict". Where two of three sources agree and the third differs, the credit rule makes the value decided-by-the-first-agreeing source and the conflict rule makes it a conflict; the section states no rule for the mixed case

response_events.note: The archive is named as a fourth source, for the unit, with its place in the precedence order; the separate unit-equality clause is replaced by one that follows from the outcome definitions.
Each value now has exactly one outcome per signal: decided when every source that gives a value agrees, conflict when two differ, undecided when none gives one; credit applies only to decided values.
